The Nifty 50 closed at 25,819.25, up 1.85% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 1.17%. Gains were broad‑based: 269 stocks advanced versus 226 declines, giving a breadth score of 64.3 (a “healthy” market). Both the Nifty 50 and Bank Nifty posted near‑2% rises, and the India VIX, a volatility gauge, slipped marginally to 17.7, indicating calmer trading.  

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought a net ₹4,479 crn today, extending a 19‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) were net sellers of ₹4,019 crn. In futures, FIIs were net short 85,230 contracts but added 5,719 contracts versus the prior session. Options data show a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.91 for Nifty and 0.87 for Bank Nifty, suggesting slightly more call (bullish) interest. The “max‑pain” levels – 25,700 for Nifty and 63,500 for Bank Nifty – are near the current prices, and support walls sit at 25,500 (Nifty) and 65,000 (Bank Nifty).  

Watch the 25,641 S1 support and 25,974 pivot on Nifty; a break below S1 could test the 25,500 put wall. For Bank Nifty, the 63,257 S1 and 63,695 pivot are key. Key headlines to monitor include foreign inflows lifting the rupee, RBI’s potential rate move, and global AI‑related sell‑offs that could affect sentiment. Keep an eye on sector leaders such as PSU and private banks, FMCG and auto, which are driving the rally.
